USB package (14 Oct 2026; distribution only, the module source and version are unchanged): loads over USB on the Modwerk beta base as an independent machine package. Its chooser row, page and renderer go through the base’s machine table, and its 909/808 DSP engine is resident in the base on both cores. The base admits this exact package through a trust row built into it; its renderer writes only under the base’s write lease and renders silent until the base has reset and enabled the engine, whose reset restores its authored tables. It needs that exact base; with an older base the site asks for a base update first. Its compiled bytes that coincide with stock are copied at install from bytes the base checks against its running stock, so the package carries no stock bytes.

USB package limits: removing it converts its tracks back to FLEX in every known Part copy and fails closed otherwise. Host tests only (the base’s reset, enable, lease and removal against a modelled DSP receiver); no emulator or hardware run of this package. The owner waived hardware evidence for this exact version’s USB package for the beta.

Site sync on the beta base (beta test run 2, 14 Oct 2026; the package is unchanged): removing it while its controller runs no longer ends the sync with “The Octatrack refused this step.” The base answers the first removal busy while it stops the controller and drops the staged package; the site now stages it again, as it does for the base's other busy refusals. Checked on a development twin through the development link (Sidechain installed, running, removed in one command) and by the site's tests; the site's own path has not run on the unit yet.

USB package bound to the new beta base acf91e0a (beta test run 2, 14 Oct 2026, rebuilt 15 Oct with the resident engines placed on demand, BBD Delay's chooser row and a startup without the wave's outline; the base's addresses moved, so the package is relinked against them, its module code unchanged and not yet run on hardware): the base now puts a removed machine's per-track routines back to stock, shows what a picked effect took and each core's DSP budget (the STATUS page's new DSP rows; DSP FULL comes from it), and no longer refuses effect picks for a bank whose Parts never fitted. A tester base from before needs the base update first.

Beta base fix (beta finding 24, 15 Oct 2026; the package bytes are unchanged): an Analog BD track in the current bank no longer silences the unit after a reboot. The base validated the battery-backed Parts before its saved module set reinstalled Analog BD, so stock judged the track's 12 parameter bytes as FLEX values and refused the whole restore: the bank stayed empty (every track STATIC, nothing playing), and the check had already clamped those bytes in the battery copy. The base now keeps Analog BD's (and FM Synth's) bytes away from that check even before the module is back; the track reads FLEX and renders silent until Analog BD returns, and choosing another machine for it puts stock's FLEX defaults back first.

Beta base fix limits (finding 24): Checked by host tests and on the emulator (boot with an Analog BD track in the battery copy: refused and silent on base 43fe3fc4, restored and every track bound on the fixed development base); the unit run is pending. Stock firmware or an older base still refuses such a bank at power-up (seen on the unit as BANK UNAVAILABLE until LOAD PROJECT); keep a separate project copy for them.

USB package bound to the new beta base a408c505 (22 Oct 2026; the module source and version are unchanged): its 909/808 DSP engine and its tables now travel in this package (ABI 10) instead of in the base. The base keeps only the engine's hook site, one placement word and its X region, and admits the package by a trust row that pins only the package's ColdFire part, so a later DSP-only update of Analog BD installs over USB without a new base. The engine is the base's earlier resident engine word for word (checked on both cores when the package is built); the ColdFire code differs only in the two base addresses it calls.

USB package limits (a408c505): checked by host tests (the loader, the controller board and the receiver against a modelled DSP, including a DSP-only update under the same trust row and a return to the earlier package) and in the DSP interpreter (the placed engine bit-exact at two places, beside Sidechain and the key bus). Not yet run on hardware with this base. A base older than a408c505 refuses the package; the site asks for the base update first.
